text:
Talent marks balanced Class A teams

By Don Lindstrom
State Journal sports reporter

Milwaukee North’s Robert Duck-
ett, a rugged-looking 6-foot-4, 206-
pound sophomore, and little Jarvis
Ashley, a point-guard who averages 15
points a game and whose smile seems
to light up the University of Wisconsin
Field House, walked along the prac-
tice court Wednesday afternoon.
“Hey! Has Madison La Follette
been out here yet? We want to see this
super guy — Rick Olson,” said Ashley.
“Awh! They’ve already practiced. Ol-
son’s supposed to set a scoring record
with his first state tournament basket.
Well, we’ll cut him down tomorrow.
Coach is going to stay undefeated at
state.”
Duckett and Ashley reflect the
strong confidence of the Milwaukee
Area Conference Blue Devils, as they
look for their second Wisconsin Inter-
scholastic Athletic Association state
Class A boys’ basketball championship
in three years, and hope to keep alive
a perfect 3-0 state tourney record for
their popular coach, Garmer Currie.
The Blue Devils and other players
may be sure of their respective teams’
success, but for most unbiased observ-
ers the choice is up in the air.
Undefeated Stevens Point? Light-
ning-quick North? Or, maybe deadly

MAR 18 1982

Class A

shooting La Follette? How about
rangy South Milwaukee? Perhaps the
winner of the Sheboygan South-
Shawano game, or maybe dark horses
like Brown Deer or Lake Geneva
Badger?
If ever there was a state towrna-
ment without a Class A favorite, it’s
the 67th annual classic opening today

at the Field House. Answer time won't «

come until Saturday night. Now it’s
question time, and every coach is
hedging about a favorite in the 1982
version of March Madness.
Coaches don’t like being “experts,”
because so-called experts are often
wrong, So, there’s a reason for reluc-

he Coshetb tl Tournament

tance, though one thing is certain.
They all look with envy at Class C
Kohler and its prized player, 6-foot-
10% Joe Wolf with his 32-point aver-
age.
Stevens Point holds the only Class
A perfect record at 22-0. Brown Deer
lost just once and Shawano, with a
marvelous basketball tradition, has
just two losses — by one-point mar-

gins. It’s a tournament with a “no-

favorite” look.
The top-ranked Stevens Point Pan-

thers drew most nominations — but -

only because of their record. Panther
Coach John Schell, veteran state tour-
nament basketball player with Cum-
berland in 1965, had a quick answer:

“You can’t pick favorites down.

here. The fact that we’re the only un-
defeated team doesn’t mean a thing.
We made it as a team, with no ‘I’ on it,
and I’m proud — win or lose.”
Predictions of a wide-open tourna-
ment are refreshingly new. This one, it
seems, has top-drawer talent. That’s
why it’s very attractive.
Some of those top-drawer Class A
stars are Olson, Lake Geneva’s Gary
Ruch, Brown Deer's Derrick Rogers,
Point’s 6-7 Jay Laszewski and Todd
Barnes, South Milwaukee’s Joe Finn,
Shawano’s Greg Polzin, Sheboygan
South’s Keith Leonard and the hustling
Ashley.

The predictions will start being
tested at 1:05 p.m. today when Lake
Geneva (19-3) opens against Brown
Deer (21-1), and Madison La Follette
(17-5) faces Milwaukee North (15-7) at
2:45. Tonight’s session has Shawano
(20-2) playing Sheboygan South (15-7)
at 7:05 and South Milwaukee (19-3)
against Stevens Point (22-0).

Brown Deer’s Keith Peters, once a
state Class C championship coach in
Alaska, has led the Falcons to their
first winning season in almost two de-
cades. He offered two answers to the
prediction question:
“Are you asking me. who’s the
favorite or who I think will win? The
favorite, by record, should be Stevens
Point. But, you know I think the win-
ner might come from the Sheboygan
South-Shawano game. Shawano’s
good, with a great tradition, and
South’s record is deceiving. They’re
coming out of a league that probably
was at its toughest in years.”

Shawano’s Norm Davis looks to-
ward Milwaukee and Madison, and
warns not to overlook South Milwau-
kee. “I always lean toward the two big
cities with teams like North and La
Follette,” Davis said. “They’re usually
talented and scrappy. But, Stevens
Point still has to be impressive.
La Follette’s Pete Olson, whose Big

Eight Conference player of the year,
Rick Olson, is averaging 28 points a
game, agrees, in part, with Davis.
“In recent years, Milwaukee-area
teams have been very good,” Olson
said. “Stevens Point’s numbers are im-
pressive, but all we’re thinking about
is North. If we shoot well, we could
win it all.”
“Stevens Point!” says South Mil-
waukee’s Don Karnowski, with em-
phasis. The Rocket coach, however,
admitted his choice is easy because
his Milwaukee Suburban Conference
team plays the Panthers first. “They
have the record and the top ranking.
We have a tough team and its success
didn’t surprise me, but we're con-
cerned with Point.”
Currie, however, is looking to the
winner of the La Follette-North game.
“We're ready after beating our-
selves in several games this year. If
we can get by La Follette .. Well,
that’s the game for us,” he said.

Tradition has proven that few fa-
vored teams emerge as champions.
Manitowoc fell two years ago, and La
Crosse Central’s once-beaten Raiders
didn’t live up to expectations in 1979.
Last year, Milwaukee Madison, with
five losses and a dark horse role, won
it all before relinquishing the title
later because of a player-eligibility

rule,
Despite that upset tradition,
Sheboygan South’s Bob Ryskoski,
whose two sons, Keith and Scott, play
for the Redmen, also leaned toward
Point.
“We had a slow start, and our seven
losses are deceiving,” Ryskoski said: ©
“We're playing best right now, but I
guess you still have to go with Point.”

Lake Geneva’s Jerry Stelse was as
undecided as any of his colleagues.
Yet, he figures his Badgers have a
chance, and if it should come down to
free-throw shooting, 6-4 Gary Ruch
and 6-3 Tim Schneider may give
Stelse’s team the edge. They hit 41
points between them in the sectional.

La Follette wouldn’t trade its
deadly Shooting Olson for anyone at
the line. The 6-1 senior guard is an 86
percent free-throw shooter. He ard
the Lancers will be the sentimental
favorites in Madison after pulling out
a pair of stunning last-second regional
and sectional victories over Stoughton
and Madison West.

“There are some dandies down
here,” said Lancer Coach Olson
“That's what makes it a state tourna-
ment.”
So it all begins today — without.a
favorite, but with a lot of king- sized
hopes.
